name: allProps
signature: function allProps(obj: any, opt: string = 'tvp', depth = 6): GenObj | [] | string | boolean

description.brief: Inspects an object to get as many properties as possible, optionally with values, types, or both - optionally filtered by props.
description.detailed: This function performs a deep inspection of an object, retrieving its properties along with their values and types. It can handle various types of inputs, including non-objects, and can recurse through nested objects up to a specified depth. The function's behavior changes based on the 'opt' parameter, which determines what information is returned for each property. It can filter out certain built-in properties and handle special cases like built-in objects. The function also deals with potential errors during property access.

params.name: obj
params.description: The object to inspect. Can be of any type, including primitives, arrays, or complex objects.

params.name: opt
params.description: A string containing options for the inspection. 'v' includes the raw value, 'p' includes a parsed, readable value, 't' includes the value type, and 'f' includes full property details without filtering.

params.name: depth
params.description: The maximum depth to recurse when inspecting nested objects. Prevents infinite recursion for circular references.

relatedFunctions.name: typeOf
relatedFunctions.description: Used to determine the type of values in the object

relatedFunctions.name: isParsed
relatedFunctions.description: Used to check if a value needs further parsing

relatedFunctions.name: isBuiltIn
relatedFunctions.description: Used to identify built-in JavaScript objects

relatedFunctions.name: filterProps
relatedFunctions.description: Used to filter out certain properties when the 'f' option is not specified

code: const obj = { a: 1, b: 'string', c: { nested: true } };

exampleUsages.description: Using custom options to get only types
code: const obj = { a: 1, b: 'string', c: { nested: true } };

asyncConsiderations: This function is synchronous and does not involve any asynchronous operations.
parameterInterdependencies: The 'opt' parameter affects how the function processes the 'obj' parameter. The 'depth' parameter is used in recursive calls to limit the depth of inspection for nested objects.

errors.description: The function may throw an exception if there's an error accessing a property of the object. These exceptions are caught and returned as error messages in the result.

return.description: The return value varies based on the input and options. For non-objects, it returns a string describing the type. For objects, it returns either an array of property names or an object containing detailed information about each property, depending on the 'opt' parameter. In case of errors or reaching the maximum depth, it returns a string describing the issue.

notes: This function is designed to be flexible and handle various types of inputs, including edge cases.
It uses recursion to handle nested objects, which could potentially lead to stack overflow for deeply nested structures.
The function includes error handling to prevent crashes when accessing properties fails.
todos: Consider implementing a non-recursive version to handle very deep object structures.
Add more comprehensive type checking for better TypeScript support.

edgeCases.consequence: The function will stop recursing when it reaches the maximum depth, preventing an infinite loop.

example: const obj = { get a() { throw new Error('Cannot access'); } };
edgeCases.consequence: The function will catch the error and include an error message in the result for that property.
The function will identify built-in objects and handle them specially, returning their name instead of recursing into their properties.
